parts.name: frame steel

physics.Basic_description: Dark grey, matte-finished metal component forming the main body, including the head frame and the long cylindrical handle shaft.
physics.Functional_description: Provides the structural backbone of the wrench, housing the adjustment mechanism and transmitting torque from the handle to the jaws.
physics.Grasped_description: A gripper can grasp the cylindrical handle shaft firmly to apply leverage, or hold the head frame to stabilize the tool during adjustment.
physics.reason: Standard pipe wrenches of this size are typically cast as solid metal pieces for strength, though the handle may be tubular; modeled as predominantly solid given the mass and category.

parts.name: handle tube

physics.Basic_description: Green-colored segment in the mask corresponding to the underlying handle tube area, appearing as a dark grey textured surface in RGB, likely a rubberized coating.
physics.Functional_description: Serves as the base layer for the grip ribs, providing cushioning and friction between the user's hand and the metal handle.
physics.Grasped_description: This is the primary contact point for a human or robot gripper to hold the tool securely without slipping.
physics.reason: Modeled as a solid coating or sleeve around the handle shaft.

parts.name: grip rib 0

physics.Basic_description: Blue-colored segments in the mask representing the raised ridges on the handle, appearing as dark grey rings in RGB, designed for high friction.
physics.Functional_description: Increases the coefficient of friction and provides tactile feedback to prevent the user's hand from slipping during high-torque operations.
physics.Grasped_description: The ribs interlock with gripper fingers or conform to soft grippers to ensure a non-slip hold.
physics.reason: These are small, solid protrusions molded onto the handle.

parts.name: jaw steel

physics.Basic_description: Yellow-colored segment in the mask, appearing as a dark grey metallic block with serrated teeth in RGB, located within the wrench head.
physics.Functional_description: Slides vertically to adjust the jaw opening size and bites into the workpiece (pipe/nut) to transmit rotational force.
physics.Grasped_description: Not intended for grasping; manipulating this part directly would interfere with the tool's function and risk injury.
physics.reason: Must be solid hardened steel to withstand high compressive and shear forces without deforming.

parts.description: Yellow-colored segment in the mask, appearing as a dark grey metallic block with serrated teeth in RGB, located within the wrench head.
parts.function: Slides vertically to adjust the jaw opening size and bites into the workpiece (pipe/nut) to transmit rotational force.

parts.name: nut knurled

physics.Basic_description: Orange-colored segment in the mask, appearing as a dark grey knurled wheel in RGB, situated on the side of the wrench head.
physics.Functional_description: Rotates to drive the threaded rod connected to the movable jaw, allowing precise adjustment of the grip width.
physics.Grasped_description: A gripper could pinch the knurled edges to rotate the nut and adjust the jaw, though this requires fine motor control.
physics.reason: Typically a solid or thick-walled forged metal component to handle the threading forces.

simulation.collision: CoACD convex decomposition of concave source collision meshes (relative tolerance 0.03–0.05)
simulation.inertia: Source URDF link inertials; missing inertials use geometry-derived defaults (density 1000 kg/m³)
simulation.friction: Source URDF mu1 as sliding friction; torsional 0.005, rolling 0.0001
simulation.contact: MuJoCo soft contacts (solref 0.01 1); source restitution is displayed, not converted
simulation.material: Rigid bodies; Young’s modulus and Poisson ratio are annotations, not soft-body parameters

interaction.description: Switchable virtual joint damping and reflected armature for interactive inspection; source properties are unchanged.
interaction.rule: damping ≥ rated effort / rated speed; armature = 2% child subtree mass (slide) or 2% mass × collision radius² (hinge)

collisionFilter.description: Self-contact excluded between directly connected rigid groups, including the fixed base; nonadjacent contacts retained
